candidates.title: B.C. man uses motion-activated zombie to scare bears away from garbage
candidates.description: More than 33 bears have been killed by conservation officers in B.C. this year, including two that entered stores through automatic sliding doors in Hope and Squamish. It's led to creative solutions to keep the hungry animals away from attractants.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Data centres are unpopular in Alberta, poll suggests. Are they a political liability?
candidates.description: Janet Brown Opinion Research found in poll commissioned by CBC News that many Albertans are wary of data centres. One political expert says the province welcoming a data-centre goldrush risks alienating voters in rural areas.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Facing a 2-year wait, this P.E.I. couple borrowed $25K to get a hip replacement in Montreal
candidates.description: Neil and Janet Payne call it "Le Hip Trip." The Kinkora, P.E.I., couple were facing a wait of up to a year and a half for Neil’s hip replacement — so instead of waiting, they borrowed $25,000 and drove to a private clinic in Quebec.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Forget AI, these Ontario photographers are taking retro portraits the old-fashioned way
candidates.description: Leeanna and Aaron DiGruccio run a mobile portrait studio capturing quirky and nostalgic photos inspired by the '80s and '90s mall photo.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Details of how Tumbler Ridge shooter used ChatGPT 'far more disturbing' than previously known, reporter says
candidates.description: A Mother Jones magazine reporter says through his reporting he was able to review "significant portions" of the chat history between shooter Jesse Van Rootselaar and OpenAI's ChatGPT chatbot in the time leading up to the attack, some of which is detailed in his reporting.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Marineland belugas that died in Chicago had chronic inflammatory disease, preliminary necropsy findings show
candidates.description: Post-mortem examinations for two former Marineland belugas indicate the whales were sick when they arrived at their new home at Shedd Aquarium in Chicago. Peekachu, 23, and Rain, 20, were part of a massive operation to rehome 30 belugas and four dolphins from Niagara Falls, Ont., to aquariums in the U.S. and Spain this summer.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 6 decades of Treaty 8 history repatriated to Dane-zaa people in northern B.C.
candidates.description: Anthropologists from the Ridington family began working alongside Dane-zaa elders in the 1960s to record traditional songs, oral histories, and everyday life spanning six decades.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Coyote bite causes temporary closures in Cape Breton Highlands National Park
candidates.description: Sections of Cape Breton Highlands National Park are temporarily closed after a visitor was bitten by a coyote on Thursday at MacIntosh Brook.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump Avenue sign in Ottawa goes missing before official name change
candidates.description: Even before Ottawa city council could get around to removing U.S. President Donald Trump's name from a local residential street, it appears someone has beaten them to it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: RCMP watchdog postpones report from 3-year review on B.C. protest policing due to snap election
candidates.description: First Nations leaders and civil liberties advocates are concerned after the RCMP's federal review agency postponed release of a much-anticipated investigation into protest policing in British Columbia due to the snap election call.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Federal intelligence agency contacted as U.S. interference claims swirl in Quebec election
candidates.description: Quebec's incumbent premier says she is "very concerned" about possible interference in the provincial election by the United States.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Helicopters in Nain, N.L., being checked after 'tampering' reported, police say
candidates.description: Police are investigating after the pilots of two aircraft reported tampering and damage to their vehicles while at Nain airport.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Danielle Smith’s popularity dips as her party now tied with NDP in support: poll
candidates.description: The Janet Brown Opinion Research Poll for CBC News suggests 41 per cent of respondents would vote for the UCP if an election were held today, while 41 per cent would vote for the NDP.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ALERT says man charged with child luring used Snapchat location tool to track youth
candidates.description: An Edmonton man was arrested earlier this month for online child sexual exploitation, after using Snapchat to track two related youths and threatening them into sharing sexually explicit videos of themselves, according to the Alberta Law Enforcement Response Teams (ALERT).
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Yukon's rural health centres without a nurse for 214 days during year-long period, CBC analysis finds
candidates.description: Data provided to CBC News from the territorial health department suggests the Yukon government is still struggling to staff rural health centres across the territory.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: P.E.I. woman who lost nearly $10K in bitcoin scam wants bank to reimburse her money
candidates.description: Binh Tran has spent the last six months trying to get her money back after falling victim to a scam call.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ontario students improving in math, but scores still low: EQAO data
candidates.description: Ontario students are showing progress in math since last year, but the percentage who meet provincial standards remains low, according to new data from provincial standardized tests.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canine conundrum: This N.L. biologist has ideas on what these animals could be
candidates.description: The animals were seen on Monday around Goose Arm, between Deer Lake and Corner Brook. Videos and photos of them have garnered more than a thousand shares online, and questions about what their make-up could be.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: As wildfire season winds down, people in B.C. communities are rebuilding their lives
candidates.description: As wildfire season winds down, British Columbia communities affected are now shifting to recovery efforts, while those who lost home sift through ashes and attempt to rebuild their lives.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Feds disclose more details on Trump admin request to delay Gordie Howe bridge opening
candidates.description: The Canadian government has disclosed a handful of fresh details around the delays in opening the Gordie Howe International Bridge, as well as some information related to the cost to build the sprawling span connecting Ontario and Michigan.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Strait of Hormuz and end fighting
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting in the Middle East.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why is it so difficult for Ukraine to take down Russia's jet-powered drones?
candidates.description: Russia's jet-powered drones being used to carry out strikes on Kyiv and other parts of Ukraine are often able to evade air defences because they fly at higher altitudes and faster speeds. To stop these new models, faster interceptors are needed, but that technology is still in the trial phase, Ukrainian officials say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: China pushes back against U.S. on Iran, Cuba in UN speech
candidates.description: China pushed back against the United States in its speech at the UN General Assembly on Saturday, saying sovereignty of countries in the Gulf should be respected and urging the "relevant country" to stop threatening Cuba and lift its blockade on it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: OpenAI says its bots have interacted with multiple U.S. government sites in unexpected AI activity
candidates.description: OpenAI disclosed Friday that its artificial intelligence agents had interacted with several U.S. government websites in unexpected ways, discovered as part of an ongoing review into the company’s models’ unanticipated behavior.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Mothers crossing the Mexico-U.S. border risk everything to reunite with their children
candidates.description: While the migrant caravans may have disappeared from Tijuana, and this Mexican border city is no longer the waiting room for entry into the U.S., there are still those seeking to cross. Many who risk the journey are deported mothers desperate to get back to their children, advocates say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What is the truth about Diana? Her brother offers his view, ‘once and for all’
candidates.description: The recent publication of a book by Charles Spencer, the younger brother of the late Diana, Princess of Wales, has only added to the way in which her legacy will keep being a focus of debate and interpretation as time keeps passing on from her sudden death in 1997.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hundreds of thousands turn out for Pope Leo along Champs-Élysées ahead of mass in Paris
candidates.description: Hundreds of thousands of people packed Paris's iconic Champs-Élysées avenue for Pope Leo XIV's big outdoor mass on Saturday, a sign of the Catholic Church's enduring appeal in the once staunchly Catholic but officially secular country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump uses contested power to cut nearly $1B US in Congress-approved spending
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump is cancelling nearly $1 billion US in spending approved by Congress, the White House announced on Friday, using a rare and contested power to axe funding for immigrant services and diversity-focused initiatives.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ukraine's largest steel plant to shutter amid recurring Russian strikes
candidates.description: Steelmaker ArcelorMittal said it was shutting production at Ukraine's largest steel plant, underscoring the growing economic toll of Russia's airstrikes that on ‌Friday killed seven people in Kyiv including a 14-year-old boy and injured more than 50.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hawaii readies for arrival of Hurricane Nolo amid risks of catastrophic flooding
candidates.description: People on Hawaii's Big Island are preparing for another potentially life-threatening and catastrophic storm as Hurricane Nolo is expected to bring flash floods and extreme surf as it churns just south of the islands through the weekend.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump cozying up to Xi Jinping could spell trouble for Canada, says Michael Kovrig
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump's summit with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, was more about pageantry than policy, says analyst Michael Kovrig. Nevertheless, he says that in cozying up to Xi, Trump is undermining the U.S.'s own interests, and potentially those of Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why Trump’s potash threat against Canada isn’t as bizarre as it sounds | About That
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump is trying to lessen Canada's chokehold on potash supply with alternative imports from Belarus — but that's exposing a critical vulnerability in American agriculture. Andrew Chang breaks down why U.S. farmers depend so heavily on Saskatchewan’s vast potash reserves, and why relying on a Russian ally may be easier said than done. (Photo credits: The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images)
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Is Israel erasing evidence of alleged war crimes in Gaza? A visual investigation
candidates.description: CBC’s visual investigations team uncovers satellite imagery that shows the IDF removing rubble from sites in Gaza that it bombed, which experts and human rights advocates warn risks destroying evidence of alleged war crimes.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: In win for Trump, U.S. Supreme Court lets states use revamped voter verification system
candidates.description: The U.S. Supreme Court has lifted restrictions on a controversial federal voter database before November's elections, granting President Donald Trump a temporary win in his aggressive campaign against non-citizen voting.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why the viral clip of 'multitasking mom' at a baseball game has enraged people online
candidates.description: A woman with a baby strapped to her chest, a diaper bag on her back, and her arms full of food at a Major League Baseball game has inadvertently become a metaphor for the disproportionate load mothers carry — in this case, literally.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: AI's 'paradise of machines' a threat to humanity, Pope Leo says
candidates.description: Pope Leo XIV warned Friday that a "paradise of machines" risked undermining humanity as he opened a trip to France by posing fundamental questions about what it means to be human in the age of artificial intelligence, nuclear arms race and other threats to life itself.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Justice Department under Trump asks EU to scrap $137M US fine for Elon Musk's X
candidates.description: The European Union's executive arm said Friday it's prepared to defend a 120 million euro ($137 million US) fine against the social media platform X after the U.S. government threw its support behind a legal effort by Elon Musk this week to have the case dismissed.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Fanfare surrounds Trump-Xi summit at White House, but no breakthroughs expected
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday for a lavish state summit that was heavy on symbolism but light on substance, with no sign that a closed-door meeting yielded breakthroughs on thorny issues such as AI, trade, Taiwan and the war with Iran.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Vietnam's president upgrades Canada to strategic partner during state visit
candidates.description: Vietnamese President Tô Lâm has upgraded ties with Canada to a strategic partnership, building on Prime Minister Mark Carney's efforts to get middle powers working more closely together to confront American and Chinese coercion.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: If Trump bans U.S. diesel exports, global prices will go even higher, experts say
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has said he's considering a ban on diesel exports to improve gas prices for Americans, a move experts say would only push an already-strained global market —further raising diesel prices in Canada and abroad.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: AI 'slop' is dominating menus, as some restaurant owners turn to it to save time and money
candidates.description: Diners have taken to social media to share photos of overly-shiny sandwiches and circular shrimp, lamenting the suspected use of AI. But some in the restaurant business say it's helped them reduce costs and save time in a notoriously difficult industry.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The 1990s boy band mall tour is back, and this time it's sponsored by Gap
candidates.description: Remember when you could hit up your local suburban mall, catch a show from a pop star next to the food court and buy a new zip-up while you were at it? History is repeating itself. On Tuesday, Gap announced it was launching a collaboration with emerging boyband Just Your Type for its “fashiontainment platform.”
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Bangkok roads submerged as flood disaster declared
candidates.description: An emergency has been declared across the capital of Thailand as days of heavy rain leave the city inundated.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Brazil's Lula bans online gambling ahead of presidential election
candidates.description: Lula, who is currently in a tight presidential race against Flávio Bolsonaro, said the industry was a "cancer" that he must "remove".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Black woman found hanging from tree was dead before body was 'staged', police say
candidates.description: Tasia Fortune's body was found hanging from a tree on the grounds of an abandoned home in Jackson in August.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: South African white genocide does not exist, new ambassador to US tells BBC
candidates.description: Roelf Meyer tells the BBC that being a white Afrikaner gives him legitimacy to challenge Trump's claim of a genocide.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Republic of Ireland confirm rescheduled news conference before controversial Israel game
candidates.description: The Republic of Ireland will now hold their delayed news conference at 14:30 BST before they face Israel in tomorrow's Nations League fixture in Hungary - a fixture campaigners have called on them to boycott.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US Supreme Court allows Trump to use controversial database to check voter citizenship
candidates.description: Critics have questioned the reliability of the data, warning it could result in US citizens being wrongly removed from electoral rolls.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Two arrested after people seen mysteriously emerging from various New York City sewers
candidates.description: The city has seen a string of incidents in which people have climbed out of manholes late at night.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What is kratom, the 'gas station heroin' alarming officials in the US?
candidates.description: Kratom, found during an investigation into the deaths of two college students, has been sold in the US for around a decade.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Bangkok declared flood disaster zone
candidates.description: Heavy rain over the last two days has overwhelmed Bangkok's water systems, with more rain forecast on Sunday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why an international arrest warrant didn't stop Netanyahu's US trip
candidates.description: The BBC's Nada Tawfik explains why Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu was not arrested after speaking at the UN, despite an ICC arrest warrant.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Thousands turn out to greet Pope in France
candidates.description: The BBC's Hugh Schofield looks at why the visit is met with enthusiasm the Church attributes to growing spirituality among the French.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover
candidates.description: One of gaming's biggest horror franchises has come to the UK. Can it live up to the original?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why this island paradise has the world's fastest-growing HIV epidemic
candidates.description: In mid-September, Fiji's government declared a national emergency because of a startling rise in HIV infections. The country's crystal meth epidemic is a strong contributing factor.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pope warns a 'paradise of machines' could undermine humanity as he opens France trip
candidates.description: Pope Leo XIV has warned that a "paradise of machines" could undermine humanity. He raises concerns about artificial intelligence, nuclear arms, and human rights during his visit to France.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: There's a global pandemic treaty that's signed -- and in 'limbo.' What's the holdup?
candidates.description: The treaty aims to help the countries of the world prepare for — and defeat — any future pandemic. Why hasn't it gone into effect?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pope Leo warns a 'paradise of machines' could undermine humanity on his France visit
candidates.description: Pope Leo XIV raised existential concerns about scientific progress, life and human rights during a speech on his first papal visit to France.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump and Xi strike cordial tone at summit. And, Netanyahu gives defiant UNGA speech
candidates.description: Trump and Xi's U.S. summit continues after a state dinner Thursday night. And, Netanyahu returns to Israel after giving a defensive and defiant speech at the U.N. General Assembly.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Former U.S. ambassador to China on Xi Jinping's visit to Washington
candidates.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to China Nicholas Burns about Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington and what has been accomplished.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Netanyahu rages against critics, including Mamdani, at the U.N. General Assembly
candidates.description: Middle East crises draw major focus as the U.N. General Assembly hears from Israel, the Palestinian Authority and Yemen.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Is Switzerland's neutrality at a crossroads?
candidates.description: Switzerland is voting on whether to tighten its famous neutrality — a move that could reshape its response to Russia and future conflicts.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Iran's president says his country has 'no trust' in U.S. in meeting with journalists
candidates.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep was part of a small group of journalists who met with an Iranian official on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York. He tells Leila Fadel what he learned.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Aga's restaurant in Houston is number one in the world for Uber Eats deliveries
candidates.description: In Houston, Aga's Indian-Pakistani restaurant serves around 4,000 meals a day and according to Uber Eats, it has the most takeout orders in the world on the their platform.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why this Pokémon set is dropping in value
candidates.description: How does one price a cemetery plot? Are they using dynamic pricing to figure it out? We tackle that question and many more in this week's Indicator newsletter.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: American farmers are hurting -- and worried about their futures
candidates.description: Farmers who grow soybeans, corn, cotton and other crops are facing another year of losses as soaring fuel and fertilizer costs offset higher revenues.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve is low. Here's why you should care
candidates.description: The U.S. has tapped into its strategic oil reserve to help drive down rising gasoline prices in the wake of the war with Iran. Can oil from Venezuela help fill it back up?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How stores choose what to put on their shelves — like, say, Planet Money's board game
candidates.description: The most coveted real estate in business might just be the choicest shelf space of national big box retail. We go inside the room and the process of how stores choose what you can and can't buy.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. has more thalidomide survivors than the government admits
candidates.description: In the 1950s and 1960s, doctors gave the drug thalidomide to pregnant patients without telling them — and without FDA approval. Now those patients' children want recognition.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Meal deliveries can save money and improve health. Will they survive Medicaid cuts?
candidates.description: Some states deliver meals to Medicaid patients that address their dietary needs. Evidence shows it aids recovery and saves healthcare costs, but federal budget cuts may lead some states to cancel it.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Mom! Mom! MOM! 3 ways to stay calm in stressful parenting moments
candidates.description: Parenthood can be overwhelming. A therapist and mom of three shares techniques to help calibrate your emotions — so you can show up better for yourself and your family.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Congress passed $100 million for teen pregnancy prevention. Most of it is untouched
candidates.description: With days left to go in the 2026 fiscal year, lawmakers push the health department to spend the money Congress allocated to prevent teen pregnancy. An NPR exclusive.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: President Trump's FDA commissioner nom, Dr. Heidi Overton, faces Senators' questions
candidates.description: Dr. Heidi Overton has been nominated to be the new FDA commissioner. The Senate HELP committee pressed her on vaccines, mifepristone, food safety and whether she can tell the president he's wrong.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How to limit rat numbers? Train humans
candidates.description: No matter how much poison you put out, rats continue to thrive. So D.C.'s Rat Rangers are trying education (of people, not the rats). They take residents into back alleys to illuminate the problem.
candidates.author: NPR
